title: Rearing flock — 6wk pullets: bloody droppings and huddling
presentation: Two hundred six-week-old free-range pullets moved onto deep litter ten days ago. Blood-streaked, mucoid droppings in the litter, birds huddling, feed intake down a fifth, and six dead over two days.

stages.title: Assess the flock
stages.briefing: Affected birds: pale combs, ruffled feathers, huddling away from feeders. Droppings blood-streaked with mucus and shed mucosa. Feed intake down 20%, water intake down. Six deaths in 48 hours. Litter wet around the drinkers and capped. Coccidiosis vaccine not given; no in-feed coccidiostat in the current ration. House temperature and ventilation adequate.
stages.prompt: Which findings point towards coccidiosis rather than a bacterial enteritis?

options.label: Blood and shed mucosa in the droppings of six-week-old birds
options.detail: Caecal and intestinal mucosal damage at the classic age

options.label: Wet, capped litter around the drinkers
options.detail: Where sporulated oocysts accumulate

options.label: No vaccine and no coccidiostat in the ration
options.detail: Nothing standing between the flock and the parasite

options.label: Feed and water intake down
options.detail: True of any sick flock

options.label: Pale combs
options.detail: Follows the blood loss; it does not identify the cause

stages.explanation: Age, blood with shed mucosa, and wet litter is the coccidiosis triad, and the absent prevention makes it likely rather than merely possible. Necrotic enteritis is the differential that shares the age and the mortality, which is why the plan below looks for both rather than assuming.

stages.title: Choose the samples
stages.briefing: You can post-mortem the dead birds on farm and submit litter and droppings.

options.label: Post-mortem with mucosal scrapings from duodenum, jejunum and caeca
options.detail: Lesion scoring by site names the Eimeria species

options.label: Faecal or litter oocyst count
options.detail: Quantifies challenge and tracks the response

options.label: Wet mount of mucosal scrapings for schizonts and oocysts
options.detail: Immediate confirmation, on farm

options.label: Gross lesion scoring for necrotic enteritis with Clostridium culture
options.detail: The co-infection that changes treatment

options.label: Litter moisture measurement
options.detail: The husbandry driver, measured rather than guessed

options.label: Serology for infectious bronchitis
options.detail: A respiratory pathogen, not a cause of bloody droppings

options.label: Individual haematology on affected pullets
options.detail: Impractical and it will not change flock treatment

stages.explanation: Coccidiosis is diagnosed by where the lesions are: E. acervulina in the duodenum, E. maxima in mid-gut, E. tenella in the caeca, each with its own appearance. Scoring the sites tells you the species and therefore the management. Looking for necrotic enteritis in the same post-mortem is not optional — the two travel together and only one responds to amprolium.

stages.title: Interpret the results
stages.briefing: Post-mortem: caeca distended with blood and cores in four of six birds, petechiae through the caecal wall; duodenum with mild white transverse streaking in two birds. Mucosal scrapings: numerous E. tenella schizonts in the caeca, E. acervulina oocysts in the duodenum. Litter oocyst count 180,000 per gram. Litter moisture 42% (target under 30%). No ballooned, friable small intestine and no Clostridium perfringens overgrowth on culture. Feed analysis: no coccidiostat detected.
stages.prompt: Which conclusions do these results support?

options.label: Caecal coccidiosis from Eimeria tenella with duodenal E. acervulina
options.detail: Species identified by site and life stage

options.label: Wet litter is driving the oocyst challenge
options.detail: Moisture 42% with 180,000 oocysts per gram

options.label: Necrotic enteritis is not currently present
options.detail: No ballooned friable gut and no C. perfringens overgrowth

options.label: The ration provides no anticoccidial cover
options.detail: None detected on feed analysis

options.label: Salmonellosis is the likely cause of the deaths
options.detail: Nothing here supports it and the lesions are parasitic

options.label: Blackhead (histomonosis) is the diagnosis
options.detail: Caecal cores occur, but schizonts identify Eimeria and the liver is unaffected

stages.explanation: Two species with two lesion patterns in one flock is normal and it matters, because the caecal form is the one causing the mortality. Documenting the absence of necrotic enteritis stops an unnecessary antibiotic, and measuring the litter turns "the shed looked damp" into the number that has to change.

stages.title: Commit to a diagnosis
stages.briefing: E. tenella schizonts with bloody caecal cores, duodenal E. acervulina, litter oocyst count 180,000/g at 42% moisture, no coccidiostat in feed, no necrotic enteritis.

options.label: Clinical coccidiosis, predominantly Eimeria tenella, on an unmedicated flock with wet litter
options.detail: Species, driver and the gap in prevention

options.label: Necrotic enteritis
options.detail: Excluded on lesions and culture

options.label: Histomonosis (blackhead)
options.detail: No hepatic lesions and Eimeria stages identified

options.label: Salmonellosis
options.detail: Not isolated, and the lesions are parasitic

options.label: Non-specific bacterial enteritis
options.detail: Ignores a lesion score and a litter count that name the parasite

stages.explanation: The diagnosis dictates a two-part response: amprolium or toltrazuril in the water now, and litter management with drinker repair to cut the challenge — plus a decision for the next batch about vaccination or an in-feed coccidiostat. Treating the birds without drying the litter treats this week only.
